workflows.name: Gift Card Dormancy Monitoring, Escheat Evaluation & Expired-Liability Derecognition

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-flag of "flags stored-value balances with 24 months of inactivity" (replaces manual Step 1).
- Dormancy sweep auto-run with outreach SMS/email auto-queued and the 60-day window auto-tracked (replaces manual Step 2 dispatch).
- Breakage entry auto-drafted from the approved sweep population (replaces manual Step 4 posting).
Controls: - CTL-393 (ensure controlled execution — Gift Card Reconciliation & Analytics (PA-54.3).)
- operational: Finance Manager review and approval gate; Legal Counsel sign-off before derecognition
Pain Points / Risks: - **Compliance risk**: dormant balances derecognized without a documented escheat evaluation forfeit the statutory defense and invite penalty exposure; mitigated by the Legal Counsel sign-off gate (Step 3) before any derecognition

- **Breakage-misstatement risk**: premature derecognition overstates income if customers later redeem; mitigated by the remote-redemption test, the 60-day outreach window, and quarterly re-review of previously derecognized tranches

- **Reactivation risk**: a customer redeems a derecognized balance after the liability was taken to income; mitigated by the automatic re-liability posting rule (system re-books the liability and reverses the breakage entry on redemption of a flagged card)
Staffing Implication: - Absorbed within existing Finance and Legal headcount; no incremental staffing (the sweep and register are system-generated; the evaluation is a low-volume annual cycle).
System Touchpoints: - Stored-value ledger dormancy flag (24-month no-activity rule) with dormancy register export (links to VS-54 / W2158 reconciliation — the derecognized population must tie to the liability roll-forward)
- Customer outreach queue via loyalty contact data (links to VS-13) — the 60-day reactivation window evidence
- Legal case log for escheat evaluation & filing (links to VS-100) — the per-tranche applicability position
- GL derecognition entry with PFRS 15 breakage posting (links to VS-17 / W9A month-end close; feeds W2159 monthly gift-card financial reporting)
Time Estimate: Quarterly sweep validation & outreach ~4 hours × 4 sweeps = **~16 hours/year**; annual escheat evaluation & derecognition cycle ~10–14 hours (Legal evaluation 4–6 + posting 4–6 + filing/archive 2); total **~26–30 hours/year** (Accountant ~20, Legal Counsel ~6, Finance Manager oversight absorbed).

steps.activity: System flags stored-value balances with 24 months of inactivity per the quarterly dormancy sweep; generates the dormancy register (card number, balance, last activity, load channel)

Accountant validates the dormancy register against redemptions, reissued cards, and pending disputes; queues customer outreach (SMS/email via loyalty contact data) giving 60 days to reactivate before the annual evaluation

Legal Counsel evaluates escheat applicability for unclaimed balances under Philippine unclaimed-property rules and, where applicable, prepares the filing through counsel; documents the position per dormant tranche

Finance derecognizes eligible expired liabilities to breakage income per the PFRS 15 breakage policy (only where redemption is remote and the tranche passed the Legal evaluation); posts the GL entry and archives the dormancy register

Escheat filing executed where applicable; dormant-balance population, outreach evidence, derecognition entries, and filings archived for audit (feeds W2159 monthly reporting and the W2160 fraud-monitoring exclusions list)
